title: Definitions shared by the Pharos plugin contracts

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date and time, UTC recommended.

duration.description: A positive whole number of seconds, minutes, hours or days: 30s, 10m, 6h, 1d.

byte_size.description: Bytes, as an integer or with a binary unit: 52428800 or "50MiB".

plugin_id.description: Reverse-DNS identifier owned by the publisher, or local.<name> for a plugin made on this library.

dataset.description: A versioned export dataset, such as usage/1. A published version never changes.

field_type.description: What a field holds. In aggregate mode, min and max take only number and time fields, sum and avg only numbers, and a text or list field may appear only as a group key the dataset allows.

opaque_id.description: An identifier Pharos derives for one receiver. It names the same item every time for that receiver and matches nothing at another receiver.

cursor.description: The plugin's own value, any JSON up to 64 KiB serialized. Pharos stores it and returns it on the next run; it never reads it.

change_token.description: Opaque position in Pharos's change feed for one plugin.

transcript_kind.description: Native transcript formats an importer can drop.

namespace.description: Deduplication scope for usage records. A namespace belongs to the plugin that declares it: records are unique by (plugin ID, namespace, id), so no other plugin can overwrite them.

machine.description: A machine that a drop came from. key is stable for that machine and user within the plugin.

machine_id.description: Optional hardware or OS identifier, such as /etc/machine-id, used only as a hint for the machine registry.

drop.description: One folder of output_dir (or of a bundle). Transcript drops mirror the source's layout under root; a usage drop holds usage-records/1 JSON Lines files.

dir.description: Relative, slash-separated path under output_dir. No '..' or leading '/'.

machine.description: key of a machine declared beside this drop.

source.description: Capture source name; defaults to kind.

root.description: The original absolute path on that machine, POSIX or Windows style. A file's original path is root joined with its path under dir.

tokens.description: Token counts by category, already normalized: input that was neither read from nor written to a cache, cache reads, cache writes by lifetime, output, reasoning output, and anything the source could not classify.

error.description: Every refusal names what was wrong, so a script's author can fix it. Grant checks run before existence checks, so not_found never distinguishes a private item from an absent one.

item_version.description: When Pharos served this state of an item: milliseconds since 1970 times 1000, plus a counter, never less than any version served before for the installation. Pharos never goes below its own stored high-water mark or the receiver's max_version from hello, so it moves only forward, including after a library is restored onto a Mac whose clock is behind, and says nothing about other items or about private activity.

library_instance.description: The library's writable instance, from its library descriptor (pharos-library.json). Pharos refuses to open a copied library until Recover library gives it a new identity, and Recover library (which also restores backups) always mints a new instance, so a receiver can tell a rolled-back or duplicated sender from lost data. Opening one library from several Macs keeps its instance.

takeover.description: Names one takeover: the full send with which a restored or copied library replaces what a receiver holds from the instance it came from. It spans as many runs as the limits require.

as_of.description: The export cutoff: now minus the library's export delay. Activity after it is not exported yet.

version.description: Supersedes upserts of this item with lower versions.

restatement.description: A time range of a dataset whose aggregates changed. Re-send every period of every series that overlaps it.
